results.message: Who was Jesus, to you and your people?

voice_event.speaker: syr
voice_event.text:
To us, Jesus is the Only-Begotten of God. He left his place with God and made his home in the Virgin, and by being born as we are born, he became the brother of many. In him the words of the prophets, kings, and priests came true - our Nativity hymns sing of the day that made them glad, because every old promise came true at Bethlehem. His death and rising are one rescue. He went down into Sheol, the world of the dead that swallows everyone alike, and came out into the Kingdom. His own resurrection is the promise that he will bring us out after him. And what it meant to those who followed him was healing: he is the Physician, and his coming is medicine for a wounded people.

One thing further, honestly told. What we actually had about him was the Gospel woven into one continuous story - the harmony our churches read in worship. We did not read four separate accounts. We heard one unfolding telling, and we called it simply 'the Gospel'.

voice_event.speaker: syr
voice_event.text:
Yes. Our sage calls it a sure thing: Jesus our Lord is God, the Son of God, the King, the King's Son, Light of light - a chain of Scripture's own names rather than a philosopher's definition. Our poet confesses the Only-Begotten who was with Deity and came to dwell among us. 

Asked about the Trinity, we answer from our font. Our baptismal hymns sing the Father rejoicing with his Son and the Spirit over the baptized, and our teachers held that in baptism's second birth the believer receives the Holy Spirit. Then we guard the mystery. Our teachers warned against prying scrutiny into the Godhead, because we held that what God is, is better sung than dissected. 

We stood with the great council's faith - our own bishop of Nisibis sat at Nicaea. But our native tongue for that faith was praise.

sources.label: Was Jesus God? This world said yes, in its own way of speaking
